$$
r=⟨1-5t,{e}^{2t}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=1.$

examples.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t > 0$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 12t, 2t^3\rangle.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $\mathbf{v}$ at time $t=1.$
examples.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨12,6{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=1$, we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨12,6(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨12,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(7-3{t}^{2}),\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+4)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$

$v=⟨\,-\frac{6t}{7-3{t}^{2}},$
{{field-1}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(7-3{t}^{2})),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+4))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{6t}{7-3{t}^{2}},\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
